transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Charles Snyder.
The artificial intelligence giant Anthropic staged the biggest IPO in history today, raising
more than $100 billion dollars through the offering and a private placement.
NPR's John Ruach says the share price jumped when it hit the market.
Anthropic started trading at $111.50, a whopping 34% higher than the IPO price, which itself
was higher than expected.
That points to strong demand for the maker of the clawed suite of AI models despite growing
concern among investors about an AI bubble.
Anthropic was founded to develop safe AI for the benefit of humanity, and CEO Dario Amade
says that won't change.
We will not bend to either business nor political pressure.
Today puts the company in a stronger financial position, and in doing so, only strengthens
are resolved to do the right thing.
Anthropic competitor OpenAI is expected to list shares next year.
John Ruach, NPR News.
Despite the strong Wall Street welcome for Anthropic, artificial intelligence shares
kept falling Thursday on concern about the AI boom.
The S&P 500 dropped 2% for a six straight loss and is down more than 8% from the record
set last month.
Also, the Dow and the NASDAQ each lost more than 2%.
Trump administration, urging a federal judge to let it close the Kennedy Center for two
years, impures Anastasia Seokas reports.
Lawyers representing the Trump administration urged Judge Christopher Cooper to let the
arts institution close its main complex for a $257 million renovation.
They argued that the renovation plans have been sufficiently scrutinized by the center's
board, which is chaired by President Trump and is mostly made up of his allies.
In September, Trump renewed his threat to tear the center down if his name is not added
to it.
The next marquee event is next month, the annual Kennedy Center honors, which are now
slated to be held at Washington's Capital One Arena.
CBS will air the ceremony on December 27th.
It will also stream on Paramount Plus.
Anastasia Seokas, NPR News.
Now to Florida, where the state's east coast has been hit with more than a foot of rain
since Tuesday and more is on the way.
The area under a state of emergency, meteorologist Megan Browski with member station WUFT reports
on flash flooding being the big concern.
This weather system sits just off the east coast of Florida and will bring more heavy
rain to the eastern half of the Florida peninsula.
Major roads are flooded and officials have performed water rescues and evacuations in
south and central Florida.
More rain is expected along the state's Atlantic coast into the start of the weekend.
As this system tracks northward, it could become a tropical storm and produce heavy
rain and strong winds over the mid-Atlantic early next week.
It's fueled in part by the strong El Nino, which could produce more flood events and
severe storms over the southeast this winter.
For NPR News, I'm Megan Browski in Gainesville, Florida.
And you're listening to NPR News.
The U.S. Army is delaying the detonation of several tons of bomb-making chemicals in southeast
Iowa after public safety concerns were raised.
The detonation had been planned for Friday, but the Army now says it has pushed the plan
to Monday.
The decision came Thursday evening after two environmental groups filed a lawsuit seeking
an emergency court action to stop the plant out of concern about exposure to lead dust.
The groups are asking a federal appeals court for a review of the permit issue by the Environmental
Protection Agency.
The video game Grand Theft Auto VI has already made nearly $2 billion, and it's only been
out for one day, NPR's James Mastermarino reports.
Grand Theft Auto VI is the first game in the controversial crime video game series in 13
years.
Finally!
So excited.
GTA VI takes place in a fictionalized version of Miami called Vice City.
Real-life buildings and streets appear in the game, while Miami itself has rebranded
as Vice City in a multi-million-dollar marketing campaign.
That's just a sliver of its estimated budget of around a billion dollars.
The investment is paying off.
The game's on track to earn more than $3 billion within its first week.
And this is only the beginning.
Experts project that Grand Theft Auto VI will make billions of dollars for years to come.
James Mastermarino, NPR News.

topics.text: Anthropic raises over $100 billion in biggest IPO ever, shares jump 34% on debut
AI stocks keep falling Thursday, S&P 500 drops 2% for six-day losing streak
Trump administration asks federal judge to let Kennedy Center close for two-year renovation
Florida east coast hit by over a foot of rain, flash flooding and water rescues
Army delays detonation of several tons of bomb-making chemicals in southeast Iowa until Monday
Grand Theft Auto VI earns nearly $2 billion in first day of release
